keys.purpose: Records the privacy consent flag and date; local-only state, never a consent proof (proof lives in the SPEC-04 receipt).
Tutorial completion flag so the walkthrough is not re-shown; never satisfies consent (SPEC-04).

LEGACY, read-only: an older build wrote the raw pre-migration history array (source/baseEntries/productsSource) here, making it PII-bearing despite its marker-like name. The current code NEVER writes this key; it is read only to CONSUME a marker an old install already stored and to CLEAN it once the migration verifies, and a new run records value-free progress under open3dcalc_migration_progress_v2 instead. `persistence: encrypted_at_rest` is the declared policy for NEW writes — and no new write ever happens. DIVERGENCE, disclosed: any value an old install left here is PLAINTEXT residue (the raw history array is stored unencrypted), retained by copy-without-delete — the current code never erases it automatically — and it is declared as plaintext residue in the in-app Legacy residue panel. Never synced or exported.

Value-free progress marker for the v2 legacy-history migration (Beta5 W4.4). Its presence means a migration started and did not finish; a resumed run re-reads the INTACT legacy source (copy-without-delete) instead of a stored preimage, so the marker holds only a type and a version and never a record. It replaces the PII-bearing preimage an older build wrote to open3dcalc_migration_done_v2, which is now read/cleanup only. Non-PII operational state: it does not change what is collected or its legal basis, so it carries no policy_version bump and no re-consent.

Value-free record of the user's 'keep read-only' answer to the legacy plaintext migration prompt (Beta5 L-2). It stores only the residue SIGNATURE - each legacy key's name and record COUNT - never a record and never a value, so the prompt can stop re-asking while the residue is unchanged while still re-asking honestly the moment it changes. Non-PII operational state: it does not change what is collected or its legal basis, so it carries no policy_version bump and no re-consent. The user can reopen the choice from the Privacy screen, which removes this key.

Value-free drift fingerprint recorded when the legacy-history migration commits (Beta5 T4.6). It stores only two COUNTS - the legacy history array length and the legacy product count (or null when the product source was absent or fully converted) - never a record and never a value. A later scan compares the current legacy source against it and, if it diverges, surfaces an honest warning in the privacy disclosure without ever rendering a value. Nothing is auto-reconciled: detecting drift does not re-import or discard it. Non-PII operational state: it does not change what is collected or its legal basis, so it carries no policy_version bump and no re-consent.
Quick Start banner dismissal flag; local-only, never a consent substitute. Key renamed from the D1.0 fixture to match the shipped code.
Onboarding completion flag so the intro modal is not re-shown; local-only, never a consent substitute.
Interface language cached by the i18next browser language detector; local-only, falls back to navigator when absent.
Customer directory (name, company, email, phone, address, notes) used to issue quotes.

Encrypted browser store for the three PII keys (open3dcalc_customers_v1, open3dcalc_quotes_v1, open3dcalc_history_v2) as they are migrated off plaintext localStorage. ONE IndexedDB database holding one record per logical storage key; each record is a Wave 1 v2 AES-256-GCM envelope (PBKDF2-SHA256 @310,000) whose AAD binds the key name, purpose, schemaVersion and envelopeFormatVersion, sealed under a passphrase-derived key held only in memory and non-extractable. There is no plaintext fallback: the gate in manifestStorage refuses a read or a write when the profile is locked, when Web Crypto or IndexedDB is absent, in an insecure context, or when the user has declined. NEVER SYNCED AND NEVER EXPORTED: dataSync.ts reads a fixed list of localStorage key literals and never enumerates a store, so this surface is unreachable from the sync/export path by construction (pinned by piiVaultDeclaration.test.ts). The records hold the same customers/quotes/history the legacy localStorage keys held, so retention is user_controlled with no ceiling - and NO TTL SWEEPER exists, so nothing expires them on a timer. Without the passphrase the records are unreadable, which is a property of the key and NOT retention; the bytes persist until the user erases or deletes the data. Covered by the SPEC-02 IndexedDB sweep (indexeddbAdapter().purge() deletes the database wholesale).
Normalized customer records mirrored from the customer store into the desktop database.
Quotes including customerSnapshot blobs (name, company, email, phone).
Normalized quote records (with customerSnapshot JSON) in the desktop database.
Normalized quote line items in the desktop database; PII-bearing because each row carries a free-text item name and a history_entry_id link to a PII-bearing history entry.

Normalized saved calculation results in the desktop database; PII-bearing because each row carries a free-text name plus resultJson (the whole CalculationResult) and snapshotJson (every calculator input).

Staging table for re-homing a PII value between storage layouts (Beta5 Wave 1, migration 0004_pii_stage.sql): one row is the SEALED (enc1:…) preimage of one value, beside the AAD components it is bound to (privacy_epoch, schema_version, envelope_version) and the state/generation of the transaction that owns it. PII-bearing because the preimage IS the user's value, sealed — it is never plaintext. A dedicated table rather than a `storage` row because the 10 s persistence-bridge sweep deletes every storage key the renderer does not have, and the startup pass decrypts a manifest-allowed one straight back into the renderer as plaintext (SPEC-02 §3.1). Retention: the row exists only for the duration of the re-homing transaction — the state machine discards it at S6 — and there is NO TTL sweeper, so the SPEC-02 §3 row 12 purge is the only backstop; the declared max_days is the intended ceiling, not an enforced timer (same disclosure as appdata_temp_staging). Export: never through any user-facing path, since SPEC-03 envelopes are built from the renderer stores, but `db:export` and an unredacted diagnostic backup copy the raw file, so this declares the REQUIRED policy rather than describing the code. DO NOT BUMP `version` ON THIS ENTRY (or on any PII at-rest entry) UNTIL THE LANDMINE IS CLEARED: the AAD's S is a hardcoded constant, PII_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 in electron/cryptoCapability.ts, and the day it becomes a per-key manifest lookup a `version` bump re-labels every existing envelope's S and strands it. See ADR-001 §3.3 TODO(hermes) and SPEC-04 §6.

Retained LEGACY CIPHERTEXT for one PII value (Beta5 Wave 2, migration 0005_legacy_residue.sql, ADR-001 §3.6). One row is the pre-remediation at-rest blob exactly as it was found in `storage` — an `enc1:safeStorage:<base64>` raw OS-keyring output, or an `enc1:envelope:{…}` v1.1 self-asserted-AAD envelope — written when §3.6 recovery re-seals that value under the new bound envelope. PII-bearing because the blob IS a sealed copy of a user value and is the only retained copy after a re-homing, so it must be purgeable and redacted on the same terms as live PII. Never plaintext: both legacy shapes are ciphertext. A dedicated table rather than a `storage` row for the two provable reasons recorded for pii_stage — the 10 s persistence-bridge sweep DELETES every `storage` key absent from renderer localStorage (a residue row would be gone within one poll, silently dropping the only retained copy of a value that may exist nowhere else), and the startup pass materializes a manifest-ALLOWED `storage` row into the renderer. RETENTION IS DELIBERATE AND LONG: the approved mode is COPY-AND-NEVER-DELETE, because no mechanism can prove an old client is not still writing that row, and the passphrase fallback never replicated a value anywhere else, so deleting here is unrecoverable by construction. The blob survives until the user runs the SPEC-02 erasure flow, so retention is declared `user_controlled` / `max_days: 0` — no automatic expiry, removal is the user's erasure action — which is the ABSENCE of a retention feature rather than one. Declaring this table is the Wave 0 `history_entries` lesson applied forward: an undeclared PII-bearing table is invisible to the ADR-002 §2.3 scan, the SPEC-02 §3 purge, the §6 rescan and the erasure post-condition, while holding recovered user data. Export: never through any user-facing path, since SPEC-03 envelopes are built from the renderer stores, but `db:export` and an unredacted diagnostic backup copy the raw file, so this declares the REQUIRED policy rather than describing the code. DO NOT BUMP `version` ON THIS ENTRY (or on any PII at-rest entry) UNTIL THE LANDMINE IS CLEARED: the AAD's S is a hardcoded constant, PII_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 in electron/cryptoCapability.ts, and the day it becomes a per-key manifest lookup a `version` bump re-labels every existing envelope's S and strands it. See ADR-001 §3.3 TODO(hermes) and SPEC-04 §6.
Calculation history entries; PII-derived because entries can reference product/customer names.
Calculator settings, selected printer/marketplace, and section toggles; no personal data.
Enabled/disabled state of calculator sections.
Selected UI theme.

Dashboard targets the user typed in (printsPerMonth, buyPrice, targetSellPrice). The revenue/profit aggregates the panel displays are computed in memory from the history store on every render and are never persisted under this key.
Monthly revenue goal number set by the user.
Custom printers/materials/marketplaces added by the user (seed catalog is code, not data).
Filament spool inventory (material, cost, remaining grams); no personal data.
Custom filament color swatches (name + hex) added by the user; no personal data.
Product inventory (names, costs, margins); business data, not personal data.
Key-value mirror of renderer state in the desktop database; rows inherit the policy of the mirrored key; PII rows must be encrypted (ADR-001).
Service worker precache of static assets; must never contain PII-bearing responses (ADR-001 §2.2).
Application logs; MUST be scrubbed of PII at write time (never log customer data); egress only via engineering path.

Whole-database staging copy written by db:import (electron/main.ts .open3dcalc-import-<ts>.tmp in the database directory) so the swap can be validated before the live file is replaced. PII-bearing because the copy is the entire database. It exists only for the duration of the import and is renamed away on success; there is no TTL sweeper, so the SPEC-02 §3 store row 10 purge (tempStagingAdapter) is the only enforcement. GAP: written by a plain fs.copyFile, so this entry declares the REQUIRED encrypted at-rest policy that the code does not yet satisfy.

Operator-requested diagnostic SQLite backups (ADR-003 §2.2), written to an operator-chosen path behind the diagnostic gate. Real retention is 14 days, matching DIAGNOSTIC_RETENTION_DAYS, and a <target>.meta.json sidecar carries it. GAP: the redact:false path (electron/diagnosticBackup.ts) is a straight unredacted, unencrypted fsp.copyFile of the whole database, so this entry declares the REQUIRED at-rest policy that the code does not yet satisfy.

Pre-erasure safety snapshots (SPEC-02 §5): encrypted with TTL, destroyed after commit, inside erasure scope. Electron only — the desktop saga uses diskSnapshotStore under userData; the web/PWA webSnapshotStore() has no production caller.
Passphrase-derived session key (ADR-001 fallback); memory only, zeroized on exit; never persisted or logged.
SPEC-02 erasure saga journal: saga id, per-store states and timestamps only — never user content. Web platform; desktop keeps the journal in userData.

Encrypted rollback snapshot of the current erasure saga (AES-256-GCM via the ADR-001 capability); the value is ciphertext only, and it is destroyed on commit/rollback or after the 7-day TTL. DECLARED AND WRITABLE: webSnapshotStore().write() writes this key through guardedStorage (erasureSaga/webStores.ts), so the S1 gate must keep recognizing it — an unregistered key makes the production write a silent no-op. NOT-YET-WIRED: webSnapshotStore() currently has no production caller, so no saga invokes it yet. The electron saga uses the separate erasure_snapshots entry (diskSnapshotStore under userData).
Model comparison panel: file names, dimensions, weights and print times of models the user explicitly added to the comparison (derived metadata, no PII).
Interface layout mode preference (classic/guided/bento); device-level ergonomic choice, never synchronized.
Last used social network id (static catalog id only; share message text is never persisted).
Last compared marketplace ids (subset of the static catalog; no user data).
Active destination id and the list of destinations the user hid from navigation. Additive key: absence means all destinations visible. Hiding a destination never deletes the data behind it.

Value-free completion flag for the web re-home of legacy plaintext PII (open3dcalc_customers_v1, open3dcalc_quotes_v1, open3dcalc_history_v2) into the encrypted vault (Wave 3, HIGH-3). It stores only a version and the migrated key NAMES - never a record field - and exists so a later unlock does not re-migrate. Non-PII operational state: it does not change what is collected or its legal basis, so it carries no policy_version bump and no re-consent. The plaintext source is never deleted (copy-without-delete) and is disclosed separately.
